items.markdown:
**Opzelura** (ruxolitinib) 1.5% is `a prescription topical cream applied to the skin to treat mild-to-moderate eczema and nonsegmental vitiligo`.[[1]](https://www.drugs.com/opzelura.html)[[2]](https://nationaleczema.org/treatments/drug-faq/ruxolitinib-faq/)

### What It Treats

- **Eczema (Atopic Dermatitis):** Used for short-term and non-continuous chronic treatment in adults and children aged 2 years and older whose condition is not well-controlled by other prescription topical treatments.[[1]](https://www.opzelura.com/)
- **Vitiligo:** Used for the treatment of nonsegmental vitiligo (a condition causing patches of skin to lose their color) in adults and children aged 12 years and older to help restore skin pigmentation.[[1]](https://investor.incyte.com/news-releases/news-release-details/incyte-announces-us-fda-approval-opzeluratm-ruxolitinib-cream-0)[[2]](https://www.opzelura.com/)

### How It Works

- **JAK Inhibitor:** It belongs to a class of medications called Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors, specifically targeting JAK1 and JAK2.
- **Calming Immunity:** It blocks overactive immune system pathways and chemical messengers (cytokines) that drive inflammation, itching, and the loss of skin pigment.[[1]](https://www.webmd.com/drugs/opzelura-ruxolitinib)[[2]](https://www.drugs.com/opzelura.html)[[3]](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/medguide.cfm?setid=24da5509-6631-4795-9d42-273faecd08e7)

### Important Safety Information

- **External Use Only:** Opzelura is meant for application on the skin only. It should not be used in the eyes, mouth, or vagina.[[1]](https://www.opzelura.com/atopic-dermatitis/what-is-opzelura)
- **Boxed Warnings:** Because it affects the immune system, JAK inhibitors carry warnings for serious risks, including serious infections, increased risk of cancer, blood clots, and major cardiovascular events (mostly studied with oral forms).[[1]](https://www.opzelura.com/atopic-dermatitis/safety-side-effects)[[2]](https://www.drugs.com/opzelura.html)[[3]](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/medguide.cfm?setid=24da5509-6631-4795-9d42-273faecd08e7)
- **Combination Restrictions:** It should not be used at the same time as therapeutic biologics, other JAK inhibitors, or strong immunosuppressants like cyclosporine or azathioprine.[[1]](https://www.opzelura.com/atopic-dermatitis/what-is-opzelura)
